CHIEF COMPLAINT
New breast reduction consultation

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 25-year-old female presenting for evaluation of bilateral breast reduction due to symptomatic macromastia. She has been considering this procedure for approximately 6-7 years. She reports chronic back and neck pain since high school, which worsens with prolonged sitting and desk work. Pain has been partially managed by chiropractor for several years with minimal relief. She experiences bra strap indentations on shoulders, occasional hand numbness and tingling, and occasional nipple pain. She has activity limitation with exercise and running due to pain and discomfort. She reports persistent breast sweating. Currently wears 34E sports bra due to comfort and cost issues with regular bras. She has no prior surgical consultations for this issue and desires reduction to approximately B cup size.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for chronic back and neck pain, occasional hand numbness and tingling, occasional nipple pain, and breast-associated sweating. Negative for rashes, nipple discharge, fever, or other systemic symptoms. Patient reports feeling generally healthy.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
No significant past medical history. Recently lost 10 pounds over the past few months with goal to lose an additional 20 pounds. Attending chiropractor for back pain management.

MEDICATIONS
Propranolol for migraine prophylaxis

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Mother diagnosed with breast cancer at age 40. Patient counseled regarding baseline mammography screening recommended starting at age 30.

SOCIAL HISTORY
25-year-old, currently pursuing degree in psychology. Drinks wine occasionally; denies tobacco and drug use. Married, with husband who recently accepted new job. No current children but may plan pregnancy in future. Insurance: Currently Blue Cross Blue Shield; transitioning to husband's insurance plan (not Blue Cross) expected in July.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Inspection of breasts reveals asymmetrical appearance with severe bilateral ptosis, right breast slightly lower than left. No nipple retraction or discharge bilaterally. No breast tenderness, masses, or axillary lymphadenopathy on palpation. Measurements obtained per standard protocol for breast reduction consultation.

RESULTS
Body Surface Area: 2.65. Schnur Scale minimum required resection: 1,792 grams, which is attainable. Given extremely large breast size, potential for nipple graft noted.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
25-year-old female with symptomatic macromastia, ideal candidate for bilateral reduction mammoplasty. Patient has tried nonsurgical approaches with minimal relief. Plan: (1) Photographic documentation obtained today for insurance submission; (2) Comprehensive symptom documentation completed for insurance review; (3) Will submit for insurance authorization upon patient enrollment on new insurance plan (anticipated July); (4) Upon insurance approval, office will coordinate surgical date and pre-operative consultation; (5) Surgical plan: bilateral reduction mammoplasty via anchor incision technique; anticipated operative time 3 hours; (6) Overnight hospital admission planned for post-operative pain control and nausea monitoring; (7) Bilateral drains to be placed, removed in clinic at approximately post-operative day 7; (8) Target cup size: small C (B cup possible depending on nipple blood supply); (9) Patient counseled regarding anchor incision pattern, anticipated 1-year scar maturation, approximately 30% risk of breastfeeding difficulty due to glandular tissue removal, breast changes with weight fluctuations and pregnancy, potential for nipple sensation changes (less common unless massive reduction), and expected symptomatic relief of back and neck pain; (10) Post-operative restrictions: no heavy lifting for 6 weeks, no driving for 2-3 weeks; (11) Patient expressed readiness to proceed; instructed to notify office once new insurance information obtained.
